description: Figure 5(a) is a line chart that plots the training loss for different methods as a function of the number of training steps. The x-axis, labeled "Iteration," is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1,400,000 in increments of 200,000. The y-axis, labeled "Loss," is a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4. The chart displays six distinct lines, each representing a different model or method, as indicated by the legend: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). All lines show a general downward trend, indicating a decrease in loss as the number of iterations increases. The "Vanilla" model starts at a loss of approximately 3.4 and decreases to around 2.7. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" model starts at a similar loss of about 3.4 and decreases to approximately 2.8. The "SepLLM (n=64)" model begins at a loss of about 3.4 and ends at approximately 2.7. The "SepLLM (n=64, H)" model starts at a loss of around 3.4 and decreases to about 2.7. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" model starts at a loss of approximately 3.4 and ends at around 2.7. The "SepLLM (n=128)" model begins at a loss of about 3.4 and decreases to approximately 2.7. All methods converge to a final loss value in the range of 2.7 to 2.8.
